UnderstandingPrompt: Clan influence represents political capital, aristocratic power, the degree of centralization, and vassal standing for the issuer's clan or clans in the target kingdom. When a policy directly changes these power relationships, clan influence is an actual consequence. Centralization usually weakens other clans and strengthens the issuer's clan, but must still follow the original policy and its execution path.
EvaluationPrompt: The immediate change settles once on the game day following policy adoption; the ongoing change settles daily starting on that same day while the policy remains active. Ordinary native policies commonly change daily influence by about ±0.2 to ±1, and exceptional monarch-level policies may reach about +3. A custom policy that explicitly changes power structures should not remain at symbolic changes of 0.1 to 0.5 without reason. One-time changes: mild prestige or interest adjustments usually warrant ±10 to ±25 per clan; explicit political rewards, punishments, or transfers of power warrant ±25 to ±60; major centralization, weakening vassals, granting privileges, or widespread noble conflict warrants ±60 to ±120; restructuring governance or handling an existential state crisis may warrant ±120 to ±250. Daily changes: mild continuing effects warrant ±0.5 to ±1; explicit institutional changes warrant ±1 to ±3; major sustained redistribution of power warrants ±3 to ±6; extreme centralization, systematic deprivation, or extraordinary political mobilization warrants ±6 to ±10. Use both components only when the policy causes both an immediate change in political capital on adoption and a subsequent ongoing institution. Do not mechanically double-count the same effect or divide per-clan values because there are many target clans or the policy is long-term or permanent. Low fiscal cost does not mean low influence: judge the depth of power changes, execution authority, noble compliance or resistance, and sustained execution capability.
